questions.q: What happens when you create a table, Business Rule, or Script Include while working inside a scoped application context in Studio?
options: It's automatically organized and tracked under that application's record, with no extra step required
You must manually drag it into a folder to associate it with the application
It is created in Global scope by default unless reassigned
Studio asks you to pick which application it belongs to every time
questions.explain: This grouping is automatic and structural — tied to the scope context you're working in, not a manual filing step.

questions.q: How do Global-scope customizations compare, structurally, to scoped-application customizations?
options: Global customizations have no automatic grouping tying related pieces together, unlike scoped applications
Global customizations are automatically grouped in exactly the same way as scoped applications
Global scope doesn't allow Business Rules or Script Includes at all
Global customizations are grouped by creation date only
questions.explain: A Business Rule, Script Include, and UI Page built in Global exist as standalone records with no structural relationship.

questions.q: Why does an instance with years of Global customizations struggle to answer "which pieces belong together as one feature"?
options: Because there's no structural grouping in Global scope — that relationship would have to be reconstructed from naming or memory
Because Global customizations are deleted automatically after a year
Because Global scope limits how many customizations can exist
Because Studio refuses to display Global-scope customizations
questions.explain: With no automatic grouping, reconstructing which Global pieces were meant to work together requires manual investigation.

questions.q: What does the automatic, scope-tracked organization of a scoped application make possible?
options: Exporting or packaging the application as a coherent, known unit, since Studio already knows every piece that belongs to it
Automatically writing documentation for every table in the application
Preventing the application from ever needing a Script Include
Making every table in the application publicly readable
questions.explain: Because the full set of artifacts is already known and grouped, the platform can treat it as one movable unit.

questions.q: What's the relationship between scope-based isolation (Lesson 19) and packageability (this lesson)?
options: They're two outcomes of the same underlying scope-based organization, not two unrelated features
They are unrelated concepts that happen to share a name
Packageability replaces the need for isolation entirely
Isolation only applies to tables, while packageability only applies to scripts
questions.explain: The same structure that keeps one scope's artifacts separate from another's is what makes the whole set exportable as a unit.
